subject: Competitive eval follow-up: Redwood vs hyperscaler inference (model quality & hallucination checks)
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: competitive eval & model quality — Redwood vs hyperscaler

Hi Marissa / Neha,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good overview. Per our discussion, attached is the first pass of our eval outputs (acme_eval_results.csv) comparing Redwood's hosted model vs Hyperscaler-API-A and Hyperscaler-API-B across our customer-facing prompt set (~1k prompts). A few quick notes from our side: 

- Redwood did consistently better on multi-step instructions and context retention (nice).
- We’re still seeing hallucination spikes on certain financial-fact prompts (rows 240-260) — Hyperscaler-API-A was slightly lower there.
- Latency numbers look promising but we need similar batch-size/seq-length parity tests to be confident.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can run a quick regression check on our flagged prompt subset (I highlighted in the CSV) and provide hallucination metrics computed via your internal fact-checking deck? Also curious about quantized variants (int8) performance/quality if you can run that as part of the test matrix.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
1) Redwood to propose a short, automated eval pass (2–3 days) on the highlighted prompts.
2) Acme to provide a subset of ~200 prompts with ground-truth for hallucination check.
3) Follow-up sync to review results and discuss SLOs/pricing.

Attaching the CSV: [Attachment: acme_eval_results.csv (text/csv)]

Best,
Jordan
Head of ML, Acme Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: competitive eval & model quality — Redwood vs hyperscaler

Jordan — thanks for the CSV and the clear notes, much appreciated. Recap and proposed plan from Redwood: 

Recap of what we heard from Acme:
- Priority 1: Hallucination rate on the financial fact prompts (rows 240-260).
- Priority 2: Regression check on the flagged subset to ensure we don’t see quality variance across recent model builds.
- Priority 3: Latency/throughput parity vs Hyperscaler APIs for your peak sequences.

Redwood proposed evaluation plan (what we'll run):
- 72-hour automated evaluation across three model variants: baseline, int8-quantized, and a trimmed KV-cache config.
- Metrics we will provide: hallucination_rate (fact-verification mismatch %), exact_match / F1 for QA prompts where ground truth exists, and token-level latency distributions at batch sizes 1, 4, 8 and seq lengths 128/512/1024.
- We’ll also run a short A/B where we route 10% of traffic to your Hyperscaler baseline if you’d like to see real-time differences (requires signing the routing addendum).

What we need from Acme:
- Subset of ~200 ground-truth prompts (as discussed) with expected answers for hallucination checks.
- Confirmation if we can re-run the 1k prompt sweep with Hyperscaler routing (if you want the A/B).

I’ve attached our high-level performance summary that outlines the metrics we’ll produce. Proposed timeline: start evaluation Wednesday (7/1), initial results by EOD Friday (7/3), sync the following Monday. Use this calendly if you want a tighter slot: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/30

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-performance-summary.pdf (application/pdf)]

Rishi / Neha — tagging you for any technical constraints or additional metric suggestions.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: competitive eval & model quality — Redwood vs hyperscaler

Jordan — quick technical note from the SE side on the eval matrix and hallucination checks we recommend running: 

Suggested eval prompts / checks (we can run these out of the box if you share the dataset subset):
- Fact-checking set: short Q/A prompts with verifiable numeric answers (bank totals, KPI values) — we compute hallucination_rate as % answers not matching ground truth after normalization.
- Multi-step instructions: compare step-completion consistency over chained instructions (we’ll use a BLEU-like sequence match plus manual spot-checks).
- Context-window retention: give a 6–8 turn conversation and measure fidelity to earlier facts.
- Safety/regulatory checks: PII redaction prompts if you want to stress test privacy behavior.

Technical notes:
- For quantization tests (int8): expect ~1.6–2x throughput improvement with small EM/QA quality delta for most open models; we’ll surface token-level divergence stats.
- Please provide dataset in a single JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected_answer (optional), metadata. If you can’t share raw customer data, share synthetic obfuscated versions — the metrics still hold.
- We’ll produce a single CSV with per-prompt rows: prompt_id, model_variant, response, hallucination_flag (true/false), latency_ms, token_count.

I’ll prep a small eval-runner and share a Drive folder for uploads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME-eval-subset

If you prefer we can also provide a short script to compute the hallucination_flag client-side and send us results — up to you on data sharing preference.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Sharma <priya@acme-analytics.com>

Propose a follow-up sync Monday 7/6 at 10am PT to review preliminary results — Marissa, does that work?

Thanks,
Priya
